cases.sentence: Мать его была в молодости блестящая ___, имевшая во время замужества, и в особенности после, много романов, известных всему свету.
cases.explain: «светская женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Vronsky had never had a real home life. His mother had been in her youth a brilliant society woman, who had had during her married life, and still more afterwards, many love affairs notorious in the whole fashionable world. His father he scarcely remembered, and he had been educated in the Corps of Pages.

cases.sentence: Отца своего он почти не помнил и был воспитан в ___.
cases.explain: «Пажеском корпусе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Vronsky had never had a real home life. His mother had been in her youth a brilliant society woman, who had had during her married life, and still more afterwards, many love affairs notorious in the whole fashionable world. cases.sentence: Выйдя очень молодым ___ из школы, он сразу попал в колею богатых петербургских военных.
cases.explain: «блестящим офицером» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Leaving the school very young as a brilliant officer, he had at once got into the circle of wealthy Petersburg army men. Although he did go more or less into Petersburg society, his love affairs had always hitherto been outside it.

cases.sentence: Выйдя очень молодым блестящим офицером из школы, он сразу попал в колею богатых ___.
cases.explain: «петербургских военных» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Leaving the school very young as a brilliant officer, he had at once got into the circle of wealthy Petersburg army men. Although he did go more or less into Petersburg society, his love affairs had always hitherto been outside it.

cases.sentence: Хотя он и ездил изредка в ___, все любовные интересы его были вне света.
cases.explain: «петербургский свет» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Leaving the school very young as a brilliant officer, he had at once got into the circle of wealthy Petersburg army men. Although he did go more or less into Petersburg society, his love affairs had always hitherto been outside it.

cases.sentence: Хотя он и ездил изредка в петербургский свет, все ___ его были вне света.
cases.explain: «любовные интересы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Leaving the school very young as a brilliant officer, he had at once got into the circle of wealthy Petersburg army men. Although he did go more or less into Petersburg society, his love affairs had always hitherto been outside it.

cases.sentence: Он не только не любил семейной жизни, но в семье, и в особенности в муже, по тому ___ холостого мира, в котором он жил, он представлял себе нечто чуждое, враждебное, а всего более – смешное.
cases.explain: «общему взгляду» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Marriage had never presented itself to him as a possibility. He not only disliked family life, but a family, and especially a husband was, in accordance with the views general in the bachelor world in which he lived, conceived as something alien, repellant, and, above all, ridiculous. But though Vronsky had not the least suspicion what the parents were saying, he felt on coming away from the Shtcherbatskys’ that the secret spiritual bond which existed between him and Kitty had grown so much stronger that evening that some step must be taken. But what step could and ought to be taken he could not imagine.

cases.sentence: И он задумался о том, где ему окончить ___.
cases.explain: «нынешний вечер» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Well, what then? Oh, nothing. It’s good for me, and good for her.” And he began wondering where to finish the evening.
